findings.title: Account 'backup' has an empty password and SSH permits empty passwords
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The 'backup' account has no password, and the effective sshd configuration allows empty-password logins with password authentication enabled.
findings.impact: Anyone who can reach SSH can log in as 'backup' without credentials.
findings.remediation: Lock the account (sudo passwd -l backup), set 'PermitEmptyPasswords no' and reload sshd. Review authentication logs for prior logins.
findings.verification: sudo sshd -T | grep permitemptypasswords  -> no; sudo passwd -S backup  -> L
findings.severity_rationale: Critical: unauthenticated remote access, directly observed in two independent settings.

evidence.description: Account flags and sshd settings (sample, no hashes)

references.source: MITRE CWE: Empty Password in Configuration File

findings.title: SMBv1 server protocol is enabled
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The SMB 1.0 server component is enabled. SMBv1 lacks modern integrity and encryption protections and is deprecated by Microsoft.
findings.impact: SMBv1 has been used by wormable malware (e.g. WannaCry via MS17-010). If a related patch is missing, remote code execution may be possible.
findings.remediation: Disable SMBv1 after confirming no legacy clients depend on it: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol (run by an administrator during a change window, not by this tool).
findings.verification: Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select EnableSMB1Protocol should return False.
findings.severity_rationale: High: configuration directly observed and network-exposed; not Critical because MS17-010 patch status is assessed separately.

references.identifier: MS-SecBaseline: Configure SMB v1 server = Disabled

findings.title: SSH permits direct root login with a password
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The effective sshd configuration has PermitRootLogin yes and PasswordAuthentication yes.
findings.impact: Attackers can target the root account directly with password guessing; a successful guess grants full control and bypasses per-user accountability.
findings.remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' (or 'prohibit-password') and 'PasswordAuthentication no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/, then reload sshd.
findings.severity_rationale: High: directly observed, remotely reachable, targets the most privileged account.

references.identifier: CIS Ubuntu Linux: Ensure sshd PermitRootLogin is disabled
references.source: CIS Benchmark (title only; content licensed separately)

findings.title: examplelib: 3 known vulnerabilities affect the installed version
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] The installed version is affected by 3 advisories (fictitious identifiers CVE-2099-0001..0003); 2 are fixed in a newer package and 1 has no fix yet.
findings.impact: Publicly documented vulnerabilities may allow attackers to compromise software that uses the library.
findings.remediation: Update examplelib to 1.2-1ubuntu0.5 or later (sudo apt install --only-upgrade libexample1), then restart services that use it.
findings.severity_rationale: High: highest rating among the matching advisories is CVSS v3.1 base score 8.1 (sample data). Potential because the match is version-based.

findings.title: Remote Desktop allows connections without Network Level Authentication
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] RDP is enabled and UserAuthentication = 0, so the logon screen is presented before the client authenticates.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated users can reach the logon screen, increasing exposure to brute-force attempts and pre-authentication vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Require NLA via Group Policy: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Security > 'Require user authentication for remote connections by using NLA' = Enabled.
findings.verification: reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" /v UserAuthentication should show 0x1.
findings.severity_rationale: Medium: weakens an authentication control on a remote service; not High because RDP exposure is limited to the internal network.

findings.title: Security updates are pending for 3 packages
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] apt reports upgradable packages from the -security pocket. The installed versions may be vulnerable to the issues fixed by these updates.
findings.impact: Unpatched packages may contain exploitable vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Apply updates during a maintenance window: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade.
findings.verification: apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -- -security should return nothing.
findings.severity_rationale: Medium/potential: based on package metadata only; individual CVE applicability and exploitability were not confirmed.

findings.title: System volume encryption status could not be determined
findings.description: [DEMO DATA - not from a real system] No LUKS mapping was found for the root filesystem, but the volume may be protected by hardware (SED) or hypervisor-level encryption.
findings.impact: If the disk is unencrypted, data could be read from a stolen or decommissioned drive.
findings.remediation: Confirm the encryption approach with the platform owner; enable LUKS or equivalent where policy requires encryption at rest.
findings.verification: lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT and the hypervisor/storage console.
findings.severity_rationale: Low/inconclusive: absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.
